title: Dynamics of nonclassicality in a generalized Tavis Cummings model with XY spin $(1/2,1)$ atomic interactions
authors: Bouchra El Alaoui, Abdallah Slaoui, Rachid Ahl Laamara
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of nonclassicality, quantified by the Wigner Yanase skew information, in generalized Jaynes Cummings (JC) and Tavis Cummings (TC) models describing light matter interactions in cavity quantum electrodynamics. We first analyze a generalized JC model consisting of a single bosonic cavity mode coupled to a spin 1 atom, focusing on the temporal evolution of nonclassicality in both the cavity field and the atomic subsystem. We then extend this framework to a generalized TC model by introducing an additional spin $1/2$ atom, enabling us to examine the influence of collective atomic degrees of freedom. The global dynamics are investigated both with and without an $XY$ spin interaction. Our results show that, under resonance conditions, the system exhibits efficient excitation exchange between the cavity field and the atomic subsystem, resulting in regular, coherent nonclassicality dynamics and enhanced field nonclassicality generation. Conversely, an increasing longitudinal magnetic field acts primarily as an effective detuning parameter rather than a direct exchange interaction. In this off resonant regime, the atom field coupling is substantially weakened, localizing excitations within the atomic subsystem. This localization suppresses coherent energy transfer to the cavity field, leading to a pronounced reduction in field nonclassicality, while the atomic subsystem retains the majority of the quantum correlations. Notably, atomic superposition states exhibit highly irregular spin dynamics, reflecting a detuning-induced redistribution of quantum correlations. These findings demonstrate that the dynamics of spin and field nonclassicality are governed primarily by interaction mediated excitation flow and resonance conditions rather than the initial energy distribution alone, ..
summary: This paper theoretically examines how nonclassicality evolves in coupled light-matter systems modeled by generalized JC and TC Hamiltonians. By analyzing resonance and off-resonance regimes, the authors demonstrate that coherent energy exchange dictates the generation of quantum correlations. The findings highlight the utility of these models for engineering quantum states in cavity QED architectures.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamics of nonclassicality in light-matter interactions within generalized cavity quantum electrodynamics models.
main_result: Nonclassicality dynamics are governed by interaction-mediated excitation flow and resonance conditions, rather than solely by the initial energy distribution. Off-resonance conditions localize excitations in the atomic subsystem, suppressing field nonclassicality.
method: The analysis uses theoretical modeling of time evolution, employing the Wigner-Yanase skew information to quantify nonclassicality in both the cavity field and the atomic subsystem.
model_or_system: The system involves a single bosonic cavity mode coupled to generalized spin-1 and spin-1/2 atoms, extending the Jaynes-Cummings (JC) and Tavis-Cummings (TC) models. The framework is further generalized by including an XY spin interaction.
key_observables: Nonclassicality, quantified by the Wigner-Yanase skew information ($I(ho, X)$), and the time evolution of field and spin nonclassicality.
important_parameters: Resonance conditions, longitudinal magnetic field strength (acting as effective detuning), and the strength of the XY spin interaction.
main_assumptions: The analysis utilizes the rotating-wave approximation for the JC/TC models, and for the XY model, the infinite Hilbert space was truncated for numerical diagonalization.
figures_summary: The notes mention figures illustrating the time evolution of nonclassicality for different initial field states (Fock, thermal, coherent) and spin preparations, showing oscillatory behavior under resonance.
paper_structure: The paper follows a progression: first analyzing the generalized JC model with a spin-1 atom, and then extending the framework to the generalized TC model by incorporating an additional spin-1/2 atom and the XY interaction.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, tunable theoretical platform to control quantum resources (nonclassicality) in hybrid quantum systems, showing how interaction dynamics dictate quantum behavior over simple energy considerations.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: The generalized Jaynes–Cummings(JC) model de- scribes the coherent interaction between a three-level atom, defined by the states 1, −1 , 1, 0 , and 1, +1 , and a single-mode electromagnetic field confined in a cavity. The light–matter coupling, characterized by the Rabi frequency g, induces a reversible exchange of excitation: any decrease in the field energy corresponds to an equivalent increase in the atomic excitation, and vice versa.
FIG. 2: Dynamics of the cavity-field nonclassicality N(ρc(t), K) as a function of gt in the JC model under res- onance conditions.
FIG. 3: Dynamics of the atomic-spin nonclassicality N(ρspin(t)) as a function of gt in the JC model under reso- nance conditions.

FIG. 4: (Color online) Schematic illustration of the gener- alized Tavis–Cummings (TC) model. A single-mode cavity field is injected into the cavity and collectively coupled, with coupling strength g, to two trapped spins (shown in blue). The two spins form an interacting XY spin chain and are used to probe an external magnetic field of strength h.
FIG. 6: Dynamics of the atomic-spin nonclassicality N(ρspin(t)) of the coupled spin-1/2 and spin-1 system as a function of gt in the TC model under resonance conditions.
